answers.answer: Reveal the top region card to place the King. Each player takes another region card as their home region and places their Grande there. Of ten starting Caballeros, put two in the home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in the court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal the top card and put the King in that region; another region card determines home. Ten: two home, one success track, seven court.

answers.answer: In round 1, players choose who starts playing power cards. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts. Others play clockwise. A value already played that round may not be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: chosen starter; later, player who took the last turn; others clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the allowance pictured on your power card from provinces into court; recruiting fewer is allowed. This happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: descending power-card value; at start recruit up to the number; after recruitment choose an available action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King's region is taboo, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3: may take your own from the board; King's region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves up to the action card's number from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely. It may be split among these destinations, and you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Ordinary deployment: number is a maximum; move from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo, dividing allowance freely; may deploy fewer, including none.

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but complete one before starting the other; neither can be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 4: either order, complete one activity before starting the other; may decline the special action.

answers.answer: After a player's turn, lay the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. After all players take turns, discard any remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected card laid aside; remaining face-up cards discarded after every player; King card revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected; actions that move the King are the exception to the protected-region movement rule.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: King's region is taboo; it may still be scored. Actions that move the King change which region is protected.

answers.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put into the Castillo. They may enter regardless of the King's location. They leave only during general scoring; no action removes them earlier.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: any or all may go into Castillo regardless of King's location; announce clearly how many; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: each player secretly selects one board-region destination other than the King's region, face down, before the Castillo is uncovered; score the Castillo; reveal disks and move all each player's Castillo Caballeros to that one region (pieces selected for the King's region go to their owner's court); replace the Castillo empty; then score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
answers.evidence: General scoring: after rounds 3, 6, 9; stages 1–4 specify secret destinations before uncovering, score Castillo, reveal/empty, then score nine regions.

answers.answer: A player may not split their Castillo Caballeros: all must go to one selected region. The King’s region may be selected. No pieces may be kept in the Castillo after this stage. If selected, that player's pieces go to their court instead.
answers.evidence: General scoring stage 1 says all of a player's Castillo Caballeros go to one region; stage 3 says King's-region selection sends them to court and replace Castillo empty.

answers.answer: The three tied leaders each score 3 (the second-place value); the player with three scores 1 (third-place value). Grandes count as zero Caballeros and do not affect the majority counts.
answers.evidence: Region ranks examples: on 5/3/1, counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1. A Grande contributes zero Caballeros.

answers.answer: The player with 4 scores 6; the player with 3 scores 4; each player with 2 scores 0.
answers.evidence: Region ranks example: on 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay. In a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second place, which is not payable in a two-player game, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first; three players first and second; a two-player tie for first pays neither.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including during special scoring, award +2 to the sole majority holder in the King's region and +2 to the sole majority holder who has their own Grande in that region. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses: King's +2 for sole majority in King's region; Home +2 for sole majority holder with own Grande there; apply whenever scored, including special scorings; neither on tie.

answers.answer: No. Special scoring reveals and scores the Castillo's contents, then covers the same pieces again. They are not redistributed or removed.
answers.evidence: Protected locations and Stack 3: special scoring of Castillo reveals/scores its contents, then covers the same pieces; redistribution waits for general scoring.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be introduced at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and they must remain right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, without rotation or reversal.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Mobile scoreboard: Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King's region; cannot stack; place right side up, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: You may move your Grande to another region, but not to the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. The destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: another region except King's region or Castillo; cannot leave King's region; destination may contain several Grandes; becomes new home region.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You need not reveal which card; taking the visible top card will of course be apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: any one played card, including one played this turn; need not reveal which.

answers.answer: The game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins. No additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: Overview and End: game ends after third general scoring; finish all stages after round 9; furthest along success track wins.

answers.answer: Separate the action cards into five stacks according to the 1–5 Caballeros on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4–5 and Turn Structure 1: stacks by 1–5, separately shuffled; reveal top card of each five stacks each round; marker starts at 1.

answers.answer: A played power card is not returned to hand automatically; it stays in the player's face-up used stack, with only the top card visible. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: played cards remain in each player's face-up used stack with only top visible; a special action can recover a played card.

answers.answer: Use the King's new position for ordinary deployment if you use the King card's special action first. The King may be put in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: King card: put King in any region except Castillo; use current location at time of ordinary deployment. Protected locations explains new position when King moved first.

answers.answer: Put the Veto card before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: put card before you and retain it to stop one special action this or next round; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: While holding Veto, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; if partly executed, the executed part is not undone, though you may prevent just part.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: announce before execution; object as soon as starts; can stop before execution or prevent remaining incomplete action; completed actions cannot be vetoed and executed parts are not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: discard after using once; if unused, discard at end of next round.

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A fellow player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends both, since each sends three or all they have if fewer than three. The selecting player is unaffected, so their five stay in court.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Decay — three from court: fellow players send three or all if fewer; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and matching card face require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Starting with the player to the selecting player's left, proceed clockwise, with the selecting player last. Each chooses from their own pieces in any regions and/or their court, never the King's region or Castillo. No shortfall rule is supplied for fewer than three eligible pieces. The bold heading instead says “fellow players.”
answers.evidence: Stack 2 The King returns: detailed paragraph/card say each player including selector, three, left then clockwise and selector last; sources regions/court, never King's region or Castillo; heading says fellow players; no shortfall rule.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner's provinces. No piece may be taken from a court, the King's region, or Castillo. The source gives no explicit fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one from a region for each player including self; no courts, King's region or Castillo; no fallback stated.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. They must choose a region containing at least two of their Caballeros if they have such a legal region. The source does not specify a resolution if those two or more are only in the protected King's region.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Fellow players secretly remove two: secret disk choices simultaneously revealed; region must contain at least two; no verified fallback if two or more only in King's region.

answers.answer: Choose a region containing one of that player's Caballeros and return that one Caballero to the provinces. This singleton fallback applies when the player has at most one in every region. The source does not explain what to do if no eligible piece exists.
answers.evidence: Stack 2: stated singleton fallback applies if at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one; no explicit no-eligible-pieces procedure.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects a region on their disk and all reveal together. The chosen region must contain at least one of that player's Caballeros; return all their own there to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Fellow players secretly remove all: simultaneous secret disk selection; region with at least one; return all own there; player with none unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, the selecting player may choose any region, including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Pick one region to score: any region including King's region/Castillo, normal rules/limits/bonuses; Castillo pieces covered again without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed group is Galicia 4/2/0, Catalonia 4/2/1, and Seville 4/3/1. Eligibility depends on the current first value, with a mobile scoreboard replacing printed values: Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scorings, including this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 all 4-value regions: current first value is 4; printed group given; mobile 8/4/0 removes Galicia and 4/0/0 adds Granada. Special scoring rules say bonuses apply.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country 5/3/1, Aragon 5/4/1, and Valencia 5/3/2. The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile 6/4/2, New Castile 7/4/2, and Granada 6/3/1. Mobile scoreboards replace printed values, so eligibility follows each region's current first value. Castillo is not scored in all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 tables list groups, define current first value, state mobile scoreboard effects; all-5 explicitly excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; lower ranks score nothing. A tie for first scores nothing because it would normally receive second-place value. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 first position only: only sole first places score; tie for first gets nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Score both tied board regions for the most. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros than either region.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 most Caballeros: score all regions tied for most; Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and the Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 least Caballeros: compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo excluded.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each secretly selects another region with their disk; reveal choices simultaneously and move each group there. If a player chooses the King's region or the region being vacated, that player's pieces go to their court instead. The taboo means the King's region cannot be used as a source, and Castillo cannot be emptied by this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement gives affected players, secret simultaneous destinations and court fallback; taboo prevents taking from King's region; Castillo cannot be emptied.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, no more than one region away. The King card can place him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one away. Stack 5 King: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from the provinces to your court. This is separate from the 4-stack card's normal deployment of up to four from court to the board; complete the activities in either order. The source gives no shortfall procedure if provinces cannot supply two.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 The Court: two own from provinces to court; separate from normal up-to-four deployment and either activity can go first; no explicit shortfall procedure.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose on their disks and reveal simultaneously. A uniquely chosen region is scored under normal rules; if multiple players choose the same region, it is not scored.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 each secretly chooses: all players choose secretly and reveal simultaneously; uniquely chosen regions score; duplicate choice does not score.

answers.answer: Take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or the Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo. The summary expressly permits return to the original region for this effect.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 all-own effect explicitly allows return to original; all relocation origins exclude King's region/Castillo and destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Up to three total may enter: the normal one plus up to two additional Caballeros from court. Only the normal deployment requires adjacency; the two additional pieces may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 two more from court: up to two additional to any non-King regions/Castillo; with normal one, up to three enter, only normal requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one special alternative, not both: either two additional Caballeros from court or all your own from one region. Normal deployment of up to one still applies.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 choice card says choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Move up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros, but all must come from one origin region. Distribute them to other non-King regions and/or the Castillo. They cannot originate in the King's region or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 up to five from one region: own and/or foreign from one origin, to other non-King regions/Castillo; general origins exclude King's region/Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros, including fewer than three, from any non-King board regions and multiple origins. Your own pieces cannot be included. Castillo is forbidden as a source; destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 any three foreign: up to three other players' from any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three effect moves up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo; it does not require destinations to differ from origins. The any-four effect moves up to four own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo; destinations must be other regions. Castillo is not a source for either.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 any three: any non-King origins to any non-King destinations/Castillo; any four: any non-King origins into other non-King regions/Castillo. General origins exclude Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. They may come from any regions, with multiple origins allowed by the summary's broad wording. General relocation origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region and may include Castillo. The summary identifies no additional destination restriction for this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 says up to two own plus two foreign, from any regions; general relocation origins exclude King's region/Castillo and destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo; multi-origin destination interpretation is noted as not fully specified.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own only, from any non-King origin region(s) into other non-King regions and/or the Castillo. Castillo and the King's region cannot be sources, and destinations must be other regions.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 any four of your own: up to four own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions/Castillo; general origins exclude Castillo.

answers.answer: On the 4-stack simultaneous secret scoring card, the disk allows any of the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo. The card that lets its player pick one location to score allows any region including the King's region or Castillo; a Castillo score covers the same pieces again without redistribution.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 secret scoring: disk includes nine board regions and King's region, not Castillo. Stack 2 pick one: includes King's region or Castillo, with Castillo pieces covered again.

answers.answer: The mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. On the place-or-move special action, you may introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup places both mobile scoreboards beside the board; Stack 4 says introduce from beside board or move one already on board to a different region.
